query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Changing the percentage of elements in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA will alter its mechanical properties due to variations in lattice distortion and atomic interactions.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy in its as-cast state
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of the percentage of each constituent element (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) within the alloy
generation.conditions: Alloy preparation via arc melting, followed by heat treatment at 1000°C for 24 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion and atomic interactions among the constituent elements
generation.mechanism: Changes in lattice distortion influence the dislocation movement and thus the mechanical properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility)
generation.predicted_outcome: A 10% increase in Hf content is expected to increase the yield strength by 15% and reduce ductility by 20% relative to the baseline composition
generation.baseline: The baseline composition of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with equal atomic percentages of each element
generation.boundary: The study focuses on variations within the range of 10% to 30% for each element, ensuring the alloy remains in a single-phase solid solution
generation.uncertainty: The actual mechanical properties may vary due to differences in processing conditions, impurities, or unaccounted-for interactions among elements

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of Hf content in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA, with mechanical property testing (tensile testing) for each composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength does not increase by at least 10% with a 10% increase in Hf content, the hypothesis is falsified
